stories.headline: A FIGHT WITH THE HOSTILES; BIG FOOT'S TREACHERY PRECIPITATES A BATTLE. CAPT. WALLACE OF THE SEVENTH CAVALRY KILLED, WITH MANY INDIANS AND SOLDIERS -- LIEUT. GARLINGTON SERIOUSLY WOUNDED.

PARNELL SPLITS HIS PARTY; THE MAJORITY DRIVEN FROM HIM BY HIS SELFISHNESS. JUSTIN M'CARTHY ELECTED LEADER OF HIS OPPONENTS -- THE OLD LEADER LEFT WITH A FEW ADHERENTS AND THE CONTROL OF THE MONEY. BY THE COMMERCIAL CABLE FROM OUR OWN CORRESPONDENT.
stories.summary: Opponents Organize under J. McCarthy's Leadership; Mr. Gladstone's Letter; Resolutions; Mr. Parnell's Views

stories.headline: BIG STRIKE IN SCOTLAND; RAILROAD TRAFFIC STOPPED AND BUSINESS CHECKED. NINE THOUSAND MEN STOP WORK -- VERY FEW TRAINS RUNNING -- FUEL SCARCE AND THE SUPPLY OF GAS THREATENED.
FOUR BLOCKS LAID WASTE; LONDON LOSES AT LEAST TWO MILLIONS BY FIRE. A LARGE NUMBER OF WAREHOUSES DESTROYED -- A BIG LOSS IN SEALSKINS ALONE -- THE USELESSNESS OF HAND ENGINES SHOWN.
stories.summary: Fire in Queen Victoria Street; Loss £400,000

rounds.blurb: Among the month's major headlines: A FIGHT WITH THE HOSTILES; PARNELL SPLITS HIS PARTY; BIG STRIKE IN SCOTLAND.

stories.headline: BIG FIVE FINISH REVISING TREATY; DELIVER IT MONDAY; Germans Must Sign by Saturday or Face New Invasionand Blockade. MARCH TO BEGIN SUNDAY If Immediate Acceptance Is Given Signing Will Take Placeat Versailles Tomorrow. CIVIL RULE FOR RHINE AREA New Draft Provides for Superseding Martial Law in Occupied Regions. Senate Action Will Have No Effect on Treaty Plans BIG FIVE FINISH REVISING TREATY

TREATY "LEAK" IS TRACED; Entitled to Document as Red Cross Ofificial, Davison Testifies. DENIES ANY IMPROPRIETY Root, Too, Resents Imputation in Senate That Text Was "Stolen Goods." OTHER BANKERS ARE HEARD Morgan and Vanderlip Deny Having Seen Copy--Inquiry Likely to be Dropped. Light on State of Europe. Only One Copy Traced. Testimony on Treaty Leak tJAT mAY rESULT IN Inquiry Being Droppe. Root on Wilson's Course. Likely to Suspend Inquiry. Telegram from Mr. Schiff. Ban Merely on Distribution. Rights of the Senate. "President of the World." As to Other Copies in New York. Condition of Europe. Got Treaty from Lamont. Heard of Other Copies Here. Mr. Vanderlip's Testimony. Increase of Foreign Loans. LAMONT WITHHOLDS COMMENT Silent in Paris About Subpoena to Testify at Leak Hearing. SYMPATHETIC WITH SENATE. Several London Papers Like Its Action in Publishing Treaty.
stories.summary: was shown copy of treaty by E. Root, latter tells Sen Foreign Relations Com

stories.headline: TO COURT-MARTIAL GERMAN ADMIRAL FOR SINKING SHIPS; Paris Council to Take Up Question of Punishment forFleet's Loss.SHOT OWN MEN AT SCAPACrews Rebelled as the ShipsSank in Clouds of Steam, DeClare Witnesses.BERLIN SEES NEW PENALTYItalians and French Lament the Loss of Ships Destined asTheir Share. Sunk Ships on Concerted Signal TO COURT-MARTIAL GERMAN ADMIRAL Many of the 5,000 Sailors Missing. Ships Plunged in Clouds of Steam. British Hauled Down Enemy Flag. Germans Leaped Into the Sea. DENY OTHER SINKINGS. Report That Home Fleet Was Sunk by Sailors Contradicted. BRITISH KNEW OF DANGER. But It Was Practically Impossible to Keep Full Watch. REPARATIONS COVER SINKING. Paris Sees No Change in Situation Affecting Peace. BERLIN SEES MORE TO PAY. Public Makes No Demonstration on First News of Fleet.

LUSTY BRITISH CHEERS FOR FLIER; Gracefully She Drops in Plymouth Harbor, Escorted from Far Out at Seaby British Airplanes.GREETED BY MAYOR AT THE MAYFLOWER ROCKAcclaimed by Throngs in Narrow Streets--500 Mile Trip from Ferrol Made At 72-Mile ClipLeaky Radiator Caused Mondego Halt. Flying Escort Puts to Sea. First Glimpse of the Ocean Crosser. Leaky Water Jacket Brought Her Down at Mondega River. Wireless Reports to the Rochester. At the Mayflower Stone. Calm Demeanor of the Crew Excites General Comment. Navy Doesn't Want to Gamble, Says Towers.
stories.summary: tells of arrival of NC-4 at Plymouth

rounds.blurb: Among the month's major headlines: BIG FIVE FINISH REVISING TREATY; TREATY "LEAK" IS TRACED; TO COURT-MARTIAL GERMAN ADMIRAL FOR SINKING SHIPS.

stories.headline: CAPTAIN TURNER TESTIFIES; Obeyed His Orders as to Lusitania's Course -- Asked No Escort. GOT ADMIRALTY'S WARNINGS But Declines to Tell Their Nature -- Going at 18 Knots to Reach Liverpool Near High Water. SAW ONLY ONE TORPEDO And Thinks Explosion Probably Wrecked Bulkheads, Explaining the Swift Sinking. NO NOTICE GIVEN BY THE FOE Jury's Verdict Holds All Law Violated -- Condoles with America on Loss of Lives. VERDICT OF MURDER BY CORONER'S JURY
stories.summary: testimony of Capt. Turner at inquest

stories.headline: ALLIES NOW HOLD SIX POSITIONS ON DARDANELLES; Official Report Describes Successful Landings Against Strong Defense. EFFECTED WITH HEAVY LOSS Land Forces Suffered Most, but Some Ships Were Lost, One a Destroyer. TURKISH TROOPSHIP SUNK Hit by Queen Elizabeth's Shells, Fired Across the Gallipoli Peninsula -- Forts Bombarded. BRITISH HAVE INTRENCHED One Line Runs Across Southern Part of Peninsula, Which Invaders Control. TURKS REPORT REPULSES Assert That All But One Landing Attempt Failed, and They Damaged Three Warships.
stories.summary: Allies hold six positions on Dardanelles; congratulatory dispatch from King George to commanders; Turks report failure of Allies and sinking of one warship

stories.headline: SUBMARINE WAR ON MERCHANTMEN ALREADY HALTED; Order Given by German Officials Soon After Great Outcry Over the Lusitania. MAY BE FIRST CONCESSION And Reply to Our Note May Include Offer to Suspend Operations Pending Negotiations. ANSWER TO BE DELAYED Italy's Action Awaited as a Possible Influence for or Against the War Zone Order. OR A NOTE TO THE ALLIES Germany Said to Hope for a New Demand for the Passage of Non-contraband Articles. SUBMARINE WAR ON MERCHANTMEN HALTS
stories.summary: Germany halts submarine warfare pending negotiations

stories.headline: KING OF ITALY RETAINS CABINET; PEOPLE WANT WAR; Refusal to Let Salandra and Sonnino Resign Averts Revolution in Rome. TROOPS HOLD THE CAPITAL Mobs Smash Into Chamber of Deputies and Riot All Over the City. GERMAN SHOPS WRECKED Angry Demonstrations Held Throughout the Country -- Street Fighting in Milan. KING OF ITALY RETAINS CABINET
stories.summary: Salandra's resignation accepted; Marcoro to appoint new Cabinet; popular indignation runs high; Giolitti's life threatened
